claim: Ochiai ranks the faulty block higher than Jaccard, Tarantula and AMPLE on the Siemens suite (about 5% fewer blocks to inspect on average, up to 30% on single versions); the 2009 extension on 162 versions kept Ochiai ahead. Re-opened: the 5% and 30% figures are confirmed in the 2006 paper.
agent_test: On buggy programs with tests, compare an Ochiai-ranked hint against a plain pass/fail-count ranking as the S5 hint, equal tokens.

claim: The formula choice matters little: Ochiai, Jaccard and Tarantula are mathematically near-equivalent for blocks hit by a failed run; on real faults the formula explains at most 2% of variance, EXAM of formulas within about 0.0025, and Ochiai/Tarantula/DStar ranks correlate 0.94 to 0.99.
agent_test: Do not tune the formula: use Ochiai and spend tokens elsewhere; confirm that swapping formulas leaves agent solve rate unchanged.

claim: Label quality matters less than expected: SBFL still works (diagnostic quality about 80%) when only 1 in 100 fault-touching runs fails; extra failing runs help up to about 10 and then flatten.
agent_test: Give the agent 1, 3, 10 failing tests plus passing tests; check the localisation gain flattens near 10.

claim: SBFL fails structurally when the faulty code is run by every test, is deleted code, or always co-executes with other code (coverage ties); on 809 real bugs SBFL fails to rank the fault first in 83.8%, and in 22.9% of programs coverage collapses (Ochiai 2.2% first vs SemLoc 40.9%).
agent_test: Detect ties or collapse in the spectrum and then switch the agent from rank-by-coverage to value tracing, at equal tokens.

claim: Results on artificial (mutant) faults do not transfer to real faults: about 70% of earlier pairwise claims replicated on 2995 artificial faults, but about 40% of results reversed on 310 real faults (Metallaxis best on artificial, near the bottom on real).
agent_test: Evaluate any S5 aid on real bugs, never only on injected ones; report both.

claim: On real Defects4J faults SBFL is the best single non-LLM family, yet only 4-5% of faults are top-1 and about 44% top-10 (Zou et al. 2019); the Python replication (135 faults) also found SBFL most effective, with a weak effect against MBFL (-0.18).
agent_test: Treat the spectrum as a shortlist of about 10 candidates, not a verdict; test agent with top-10 versus top-1 hint.

claim: Multi-fault programs degrade SBFL because faults mask each other; fix-one-then-recompute (FLITSR) cut wasted effort 30-90% on 75000 synthetic and 326 real multi-fault versions and beat GRACE on real method-level faults. Gap search: no study combines FLITSR-style rounds with an LLM; the only multi-fault follow-up found (SA-BCL) is learning-based and was seen second-hand.
agent_test: After the agent fixes one candidate, recompute the spectrum from the remaining failing tests before the next hypothesis.

claim: Hidden measurement problems weaken SBFL: early termination at the first failed assertion (19.1% of failing tests; coverage improves in 55% of versions) and flaky tests (80.3% show varying coverage).
agent_test: Run tests to completion and rerun for flakiness before building the spectrum the agent reads.

claim: Human studies are mixed but the conflict has an explanation. Parnin and Orso (2011, opened): 24 students plus 10 in a rank follow-up, 2 bugs, Tarantula list, no mean speed-up (12:42 vs 14:14 min, 20:16 vs 22:30 min, n.s.), only 10 high performers gained on the easy task (8:51 vs 14:28, p<0.05). Xia et al. (2016, opened): 36 professionals, 16 real bugs, simulated list with the fault in the top 5 or ranks 6 to 10; success 98% / 94% vs 77%, time 11.4 / 16.4 vs 26.5 min, Cliff delta 0.80 / 0.55. Xie et al. (2016) could not be opened (closed access) and its N is unverified. The two opened studies differ in population, bug count and tool realism; neither tested a list that misses the fault.
agent_test: Not testable on an LLM directly; the analogue is whether the agent obeys a wrong ranking (anchoring test).

claim: An LLM with repo tools and the failing test (AutoFL) beats Ochiai at method level on acc@1: +19.7% Defects4J, +166.7% BugsInPy (GPT-3.5), +233.3% (GPT-4); GPT-3.5 lags SBFL at acc@3 and acc@5. Re-opened and confirmed.
agent_test: Compare equal-token SBFL-hint vs no-hint vs tool-browsing.

claim: Repeating an LLM localisation run and merging helps strongly (one GPT-4 run beat five merged GPT-3.5 runs); single explanations are accurate about 1 in 5, so agreement across runs is a usable confidence signal.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare one long run vs five short merged runs for fault location; link to the sampling-and-voting subfield.

claim: Feeding SBFL information to an LLM helps, but test results help more than suspiciousness scores: FuseFL Top-1 baseline 150, SusScore 169, TestRes 187, CodeDesc 180, all three 197 (324 student programs, GPT-3.5); FuseFL +68.4% over Ochiai.
agent_test: Ablate scores only, test results only, both, in the S5 prompt at equal tokens.

claim: Hybrid pipelines (classical shortlist then LLM re-rank) beat both parts on Defects4J v2.0: Ochiai 167 Top-1 of 835, Ochiai+LLM re-ranker 303, FlexFL 350 (re-opened, confirmed). LLM4FL (GPT-4o-mini) reports about 326 of 675 vs Ochiai 121, though DepGraph (learned) is higher at 359.
agent_test: Spectrum shortlist then LLM judge over candidates; compare to LLM alone at equal tokens.

claim: LLM fault localisation is sensitive to input order: in LLM4FL ordering changed Top-1 by up to 22%; a later study found reversing the order drops Java Top-1 from 57% to 20%, and Ochiai ordering did not beat simple call-graph orderings (32.7% vs 34.9%).
agent_test: Randomise candidate order across runs in S5 and measure position bias; do not assume spectrum order is best.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLM localisers are brittle under semantics-preserving edits: after such a change a model fails on a previously found fault in 78% of cases (750,013 tasks, single study).
agent_test: Rename variables or reformat before S5 and check agent stability.

claim: Adding SBFL hints to an LLM repair agent gives a modest gain: AutoCodeRover on SWE-bench Lite 57 (19%) to 66 (22%) tasks, 7 solved only with SBFL; Agentless drops SBFL and localises with the LLM. Gap search: the AutoCodeRover gain is one run per arm (+9 tasks, tokens 37k to 40k) and is within run noise (best of 3 runs reached 78); a 2026 study of six LLM-based localisers on three strong repair models found pass@1 down in 17 of 18 settings (-4.45 to +0.40 points).
agent_test: Only worth it when failing tests exist; measure marginal solve rate against token cost.

claim: Better localisation does not automatically cut repair cost: accurate locations cut repair tokens by up to 39.2%, but current FL methods often spend more tokens than they save; file-level localisation gives most of the repair gain and line-level expansion often hurts.
agent_test: Charge localisation tokens against repair tokens; prefer file or function level hints.

claim: SBFL needs a failing test; only 3.33% of crash-report bugs had one when filed, so stack-trace ranking (56.67% top-5) or generated tests are needed first.
agent_test: If no failing test exists, the agent writes one before any spectrum step.

claim: Richer spectra help: data-flow spectra put up to 50% more faults in the top 15 than line coverage, at 353% vs 102% overhead.
agent_test: Compare statement spectra vs value-trace spectra for the agent.

claim: Cross-paper SBFL baselines differ by granularity: Ochiai Top-1 on Defects4J v1.2 (395 bugs) is 19 at statement level with DeepFL tie handling (LLMAO Table 2, re-opened) and 80 at method level (AgentFL and SieveFL tables), and 101 of 501 faults at method level in Order Matters. The gap is explained by granularity and tie rules, not by an error. Still, no paper compares LLM and SBFL on fresh bugs with the same unit and ties.
agent_test: Always rerun the SBFL baseline under the same tie-break and granularity rule.

claim: Agent pipelines with test failure and behaviour analysis beat Ochiai but not the best learned localiser: AgentFL 157/395 Top-1 on D4J 1.2 (Ochiai 80), 78/226 on D4J 2.0 (Ochiai 32); removing test failure analysis drops Top-1 to 125. Re-opened and confirmed.
agent_test: Keep the failing-test analysis step; it is the most valuable component in ablation.

claim: Execution feedback beyond coverage helps LLM repair: LDB (intermediate values per basic block, up to 9.8% on HumanEval/MBPP/TransCoder) and AutoSD (hypothesis then debugger probe).
agent_test: Let the agent run probes (print values) as the S5 evidence rather than coverage alone.

claim: On small student programs reasoning LLMs (o3, DeepSeek-R1) find far more faults than SBFL or MBFL, while SBFL still finds a few unique ones (8 on Codeflaws); accuracy falls with difficulty.
agent_test: Use the spectrum only as a complement for what the LLM misses; test the union at equal tokens.

claim: Human use of a ranked hint is top-heavy: professionals read the first 5 in order (83.3% of 24) and few went past rank 6 (33.3% read through rank 6, 12.5% through rank 8); a fault in ranks 1 to 5 gave 11.4 min vs 16.4 min for ranks 6 to 10.
agent_test: Show the agent at most 5 candidates; check that adding items 6 to 10 does not raise solve rate.

claim: Agents anchor on a misleading localisation but usually recover: with completely wrong file-level hints, 34.5% to 100% first inspected a suggested file, and 34.8% to 95.9% of those later reached a correct file; small models recovered less (below 50% in all three Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Defects4J settings).
agent_test: Plant a wrong top-1 in a spectrum and measure whether the agent drops it; add an explicit step asking whether the evidence agrees with the hint.

claim: For strong repair agents the localisation hint has a low ceiling: gold file or symbol hints add +0.8 to +4.6 points pass@1 on SWE-bench settings, and six realistic LLM localisers changed pass@1 by -4.45 to +0.40 points.
agent_test: Do not expect a spectrum hint to beat the failing-test-only baseline in accuracy; judge it on tokens and steps.

claim: An LLM given a candidate list in Ochiai order does as well as with plain code-size order and worse than call-graph order: Top-1 164 vs about 163 (LOC) vs 175 (call-graph BFS) of 501 faults; Ochiai alone scores 101. So the order carries little beyond which methods were covered.
agent_test: Replace ranked scores by an unranked covered-and-failing set; compare.

claim: The failing-test output carries most of the signal an LLM uses: function-only 50.0% Acc@1 vs 82.0% with passing and failing tests and errors (no coverage) on SemBugs; in FuseFL the test-results prompt gave the largest single gain (187 vs 150 baseline Top-1, SusScore alone 169).
agent_test: Baseline arm must contain the failing test output; a spectrum arm is only worth running on top of it.

claim: Coverage is useful as a filter: dropping methods the failing test never ran cut candidates 79% and input tokens about 49% with Top-1 unchanged (165 of 395), using a 30B open model.
agent_test: Give the agent the set of executed functions rather than a score list.

claim: Value-based checks cost more and did not beat a plain LLM with the same inputs: SemLoc used 2.2 to 3.0 times the tokens and its Acc@1 (81.4%) was not significantly different from one LLM call given tests and errors (82.0%); about half (51.9%) of the violated constraints were wrong. Patch-and-rerun verification did separate right from wrong top lines (76.9% vs 19.9%).
agent_test: Prefer probes plus a patch-and-rerun check over building value spectra.

claim: Non-code analogue: blaming the failing step in a multi-step LLM run is weak (best 14.2% step-level, 53.5% agent-level on Who&When; some methods below random). No study applied a pass/fail spectrum across several attempts at the same reasoning task.
agent_test: Build a small test: N attempts at a puzzle, check each step claim, rank steps by Ochiai, compare with one-trace blame.

claim: Part of the LLM score on Defects4J is memory: renaming methods cut Top-1 by 4% to 9% (217 to 208; 278 to 253); reported leakage 0.41% for Defects4J and 11% for BugsInPy (second-hand).
agent_test: Use fresh or renamed bugs for any agent test of S5.

claim: Hint grain matters: file-level context lifts repair 15 to 17 times over no file, while line-level expansion often hurts (GPT-5-mini, 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks, 61 configurations).
agent_test: Give functions or files as the hint, not a long list of lines.

claim: Untested: no study compares an LLM agent given a spectrum hint plus the failing test against the same agent given the failing test only, at equal tokens and with a strong 2025-2026 model. Nearest are AutoCodeRover (weak model, one run, no test-only arm), Order Matters (ordering only) and SieveFL (filter).
agent_test: Run this comparison ourselves: arms (a) failing output, (b) plus unranked covered set, (c) plus Ochiai top-5, (d) plus wrong top-1; equal token cap.

claim: Untested: iterative fix-and-recompute (FLITSR) inside an LLM loop, and the effect of flaky tests, early termination or very few failing tests on LLM-based localisation. Only classic SBFL has been studied for these.
agent_test: Treat as unknown. If the agent runs multi-attempt checks, log pass/fail per attempt and test with a planted second fault.
